reasons: Output depends on the browser and fonts, which a simple test cannot fully check.

terms.meaning: A drawing area in a web page that code paints onto.
The drawing style chosen for an industry, such as pipes or a grid.
A way of putting an image directly inside a text string.
A starting number that makes a random sequence repeat the same way.

depends_on: JetBrains Mono and Hanken Grotesk fonts, if loaded on the page

sections.name: File setup, Motif
sections.title: Visual style names
sections.what: Lists the names of the drawing styles, each a motif for one kind of industry.
sections.why: Lets the drawing code accept only known style names.
sections.watch_out: A new style here needs a matching branch in the drawing code, or it falls through to the default grid.

sections.name: motifFor
sections.title: Picks a drawing style from an industry name
sections.what: Lowercases the name and tests it against keyword patterns in order. The first match sets the style. Names with no match get the grid.
sections.why: Gives each industry a fitting picture without manual setup.
sections.watch_out: The patterns have no word boundaries, so 'it' matches inside words such as capital and sends them to the tech style.

sections.name: rng, hash
sections.title: Repeatable random numbers
sections.what: Creates a random number generator from a seed, and turns an industry name into that seed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same name always gives the same picture.
sections.watch_out: Changing the seed formula or the random formula changes every existing picture.

sections.name: drawIndustrySheet (part 1)
sections.title: Sheet setup, grid and frame
sections.what: Creates an off-screen canvas, paints a dark background and a light grid, draws the frame of the drawing area, clips drawing to that frame, and selects the style.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the sheet its blueprint look.
sections.watch_out: The canvas is created in memory, so this only works in a browser.

sections.name: drawIndustrySheet: for
sections.title: Drawing styles: pipes to truss
sections.what: Draws the first five styles: pipes with valves, rows of solar panels, nuclear rings, contour lines and a truss structure.
sections.why: Each industry gets a recognisable picture.
sections.watch_out: Random values are drawn in a fixed order, so an extra random draw early on shifts every later shape.

sections.name: drawIndustrySheet: for
sections.title: Drawing styles: containers to candles
sections.what: Draws stacked containers, server racks, shelves of boxes and a candlestick chart.
sections.why: Each industry gets a recognisable picture.

sections.name: drawIndustrySheet: for
sections.title: Drawing styles: waves to waveform
sections.what: Draws wavy lines, interlocking gears, a molecule of linked dots and a bar waveform.
sections.why: Each industry gets a recognisable picture.

sections.name: drawIndustrySheet: for
sections.title: Drawing styles: orbit to default grid
sections.what: Draws orbit ellipses, columns, a cycle arrow, and a fallback of random rectangles for any style not handled above. It then draws the figure caption under the frame.
sections.why: The fallback keeps unknown industries from being blank.

sections.name: drawIndustrySheet (part 6)
sections.title: Title block and image output
sections.what: Writes the industry name in large capitals, wrapping onto new lines when needed, then lists up to six label and value rows with long values shortened. Returns the picture as a JPEG data string.
sections.why: Makes the picture read like a technical specification.
sections.watch_out: Only the first six rows are shown, and any extra rows are dropped without a message.

summary: Draws a blueprint-style technical sheet for an industry on a hidden canvas and returns it as a JPEG image.
purpose: Gives each industry a generated picture, so no image files are needed.
why: The header describes procedural spec sheets with one visual style per industry.
how: Picks a drawing style from the industry name, seeds a repeatable random source from the name, paints the background and grid, draws the chosen style in a frame, adds the figure caption and title block with up to six rows, then exports the picture.
inputs: An industry name, a code, a list of label and value pairs, width, height and an optional style key.
outputs: A data URL string holding a JPEG image.
risks: Needs a browser canvas, so it fails on a server. Random values are drawn in a fixed order, so adding a draw early changes every later picture. Only the first six rows are shown.
debug: If a picture looks wrong, check which style motifFor selects for the name and whether a style key was passed. Test in the browser's console.
